speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What is the upadeśa about the reflected world?
premises: śivatattvaṃ prakāśarūpam uktam — the light-formed Siva-tattva has been told.
akhaṇḍamaṇḍale praveṣṭuṃ na śaknoti — it cannot enter the undivided mandala.
svātantryaśaktiṃ paśyan nirvikalpaṃ bhairavasamāveśam anubhavati — seeing greater autonomy, non-conceptual Bhairava-immersion follows.
sarvaṃ bhāvajātaṃ bodhagagane pratibimbam — all states are reflection in the sky of knowing.
mukharūpam iva darpaṇe, rasa iva dantodake, pratiśrutkeva vyomni — face/taste/smell/touch/echo similes mark the reflection's dependence.
inference: The teaching (upadeśa) is that the world shows as pratibimba: what appears only by mixture with another cannot stand alone, so immersion is nirvikalpa, not world-entry.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Why is rasa not primary?
premises: na hi sa raso mukhyaḥ — taste is denied primacy.
tatkāryavyādhiśamanādyadṛṣṭeḥ — its works (disease-pacification and rest) run by an occult eye.
inference: Taste's efficacy depends on another sight, so it is kārya-effect, not mukhya-primary.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Why are gandha and sparśa not primary either?
premises: nāpi gandhasparśau mukhyau — smell and touch also denied primacy.
guṇinaḥ tatrābhāve — they are qualitied; in the absence of the qualitied they fail.
ayogāt, kāryaparamparānārambhāt ca — from impossibility and the effect-chain's beginning.
inference: Qualitied means dependent-on-substrate; dependence disqualifies primacy for both.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Yet smell and touch are not simply absent — what shows that?
premises: na ca tau na staḥ — the pair are not-nonexistent either.
dehoddhūlanavisargādidarśanāt — from seeing body-stripping, seed and rest.
inference: Somatic signs (uddhūlana, visarga) evidence their presence: denied as primary, not denied as existent.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Why is śabda not primary?
premises: śabdo 'pi na mukhyaḥ — sound too is denied primacy.
ko 'pi vakti iti — someone speaks it: sound requires a speaker.
āgacchantyā iva pratiśrutkāyāḥ śravaṇāt — heard like an echo of one arriving.
inference: Echo-hearing shows sound arrives from another: derivative, hence not mukhya.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What does the pratibimba claim extend to?
premises: yathā tat pratibimbitaṃ bhāti, tathaiva viśvaṃ parameśvaraprakāśe — as the reflection shines, so the world in the Lord's light.
inference: The mirror-model scales: viśva is pratibimba of parameśvara-prakāśa, nothing self-luminous below the Lord.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What could the bimba here be — is there a real image?
premises: nanu atra bimbaṃ kiṃ syāt — but what is the image here?
mābhūt kiṃcit — let there be no thing at all.
inference: The questioner's bimba is dissolved: reflection without a standing second entity — anuttara-model.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: How is the world causeless-looking — what is the real hetu?
premises: nanu kim akāraṇakaṃ tat — how is that causeless?
hetuś ca parameśvaraśaktir eva svātantryāparaparyāyā — the reason is the Lord's power, synonym of autonomy.
viśvapratibimbadhāritvāc ca viśvātmakatvaṃ bhagavataḥ — world-reflection-bearing yields the Lord's world-selfhood.
saṃvinmayaṃ hi viśvaṃ caitanyasya vyaktisthānam — consciousness-made, the world is consciousness-manifestation-place.
citsvabhāvasya svarūpānāmarśanānupapatteḥ — self-nature-contemplation of consciousness-nature is impossible.
inference: Apparent causelessness resolves to svātantrya-śakti: the Lord bears the reflection, so viśvātmakatva is svarūpa, not an ascribed relation.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Does svarūpa-āmarśa reduce to jaḍatā — and what saves it?
premises: svarūpāmarśane vastuto jaḍataiva syāt — self-contemplation would be inertness in reality.
āmarśaś ca ayaṃ na sāketikaḥ — this contemplation depends-on-no-other.
api tu citsvabhāvatāmātranāntarīyakaḥ — inseparable from consciousness-nature merely.
paranādagarbha uktaḥ — womb of supreme sound, so called.
yāvān viśvavyavasthāpakaḥ parameśvaraśaktikalāpaḥ tāvantam āmṛśati — he contemplates exactly the Lord's world-establishing power-group.
inference: Āmarśa escapes jaḍatā by being citsvabhāva-identical: the contemplating measure equals the world-establishing śakti-measure.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What are the primary śaktis and their varṇa-triads?
premises: tisraḥ parameśvarasya śaktayaḥ anuttarecchonmeṣaḥ — three primary powers: unsurpassable will-awakening.
tat parāmarśatrayam a i u — that triad is a i u.
etasmād tritayāt sarvaḥ śaktiprapañcaḥ caryate — from this triad the whole power-manifold is carried.
anuttare viśrāntir ānandaḥ — in unsurpassable, rest is bliss; icchāyām īśanam — rest in will is rulership.
unmeṣe viśrāntir ūrmiḥ — awakening's rest is the wave; kriyāśakteḥ prārambhaḥ tat parāmarśatrayam ā ī ū — action-power's beginning is ā ī ū.
inference: The bīja-scheme is doctrinal: a i u = icchā-ānanda-īśana triad, ā ī ū = kriyā's commencement — sound encodes the power-structure.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: How are the two triads characterized cosmically?
premises: prācyaṃ parāmarśatrayam prakāśabhāgasāratvāt sūryātmakam — the prior triad, essence-of-light-part, is sun-natured.
caramaṃ parāmarśatrayam viśrāntisvabhāvāhlādaprādhānyāt somātmakam — the final, rest-bliss-prevalent, moon-natured.
iyati yāvat karmāṃśasyānupraveśo nāsti — up to where the action-portion does not enter.
inference: Sun/moon marks the triads' function-boundary: light-side before action-entry, bliss-rest after.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: When karma enters icchā-īśana, what results?
premises: yadā icchāyām īśane ca karma anupraviśati — when action enters will and rulership.
tat iṣyamāṇam īśyamāṇam iti ucyate — it is called iṣyamāṇa and īśyamāṇa.
dvau bhedau: prakāśamātreṇa raśrutiḥ, viśrāntyā laśrutiḥ — two kinds: ra by mere light, la by rest.
ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt — ra and la are light-and-stopping natured.
asphuṭatvāt eva śrutimātraṃ ralayoḥ — from non-distinctness, only hearing stands, no expression.
inference: Action-in-will bifurcates into ra/la uttara-varṇas whose nature is prakāśa-stambha: heard-not-expressed, hence śruti-mātra.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Why is the ṛ-quad napuṃsaka?
premises: tat varṇacatuṣṭayam ubhayacchāyādhāritvāt napuṃsakam — the quad ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ is neuter.
ubhaya-chāyā-dhārita — it bears both shades (masculine/feminine).
inference: Neuter marks double-shade-bearing: the r-vowels sit between the gendered poles.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Which pair appears at the anuttara-ānanda spread?
premises: anuttarānandayoḥ icchādiṣu yadā prasaraḥ — when the spread of unsurpassable-bliss runs in will and rest.
tadā varṇadvayam e oṃ — the pair is e and oṃ.
inference: e/oṃ encode the anuttara-ānanda spread-point in the bīja sequence.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Which pair follows from anuttara-ānanda-saṃghaṭṭa?
premises: tatrāpi punar anuttarānandasaṃghaṭṭāt varṇadvayam ai au — from the union of unsurpassable bliss, ai au.
inference: ai/au mark the saṃghaṭṭa (union) moment — a further fold of the same spread.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What is kriyā-śakti in varṇa terms?
premises: sā iyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ — this is action-power.
tad eva varṇacatuṣṭayam e ai o au — that very quad is e ai o au.
inference: The four diphthongs ARE kriyā-śakti: vowel-quad = action-power signature.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What stands at kriyāśaktyanta before anuttara-entry?
premises: kriyāśaktyante sarvaṃ kāryabhūtaṃ — at action-power's end all is effect.
yāvat anuttare pravekṣyati, tāvad eva pūrvaṃ saṃvedanasāratayā prakāśamātratvena bindutayā āste am — until entry, prior stands as consciousness-essence, mere light, point: am.
inference: am is the bindu-state: all-effect pending, standing as prakāśa-mātra at the threshold of anuttara.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What is born from that bindu?
premises: tatas tatraiva anuttarasya visargo jāyate aḥ — then the unsurpassable's visarga is born: aḥ.
inference: aḥ is anuttara's own visarga — the seed-drop born at the am-point.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What does this totalize to?
premises: evaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ parāmarśānāṃ bījasvarūpam ucyate — thus the sixteenfold seed-form of contemplations.
inference: a + i u + ā ī ū + e oṃ + ai au + e ai o au + am + aḥ =16 bījas: parāmarśa's complete seed-scheme.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What kind of form arises from these seeds?
premises: tadutthaṃ vyañjanātmakaṃ yonirūpam — born-from-that, expression-natured, womb-form.
inference: The seed-scheme yields vyañjana-yoni: expressive womb from which the consonant-classes descend.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: How do the consonant-classes distribute over the śaktis?
premises: anuttarāt kavargaḥ śraddhāyāḥ — from anuttara, ka-class of śraddhā (faith-will).
cavargaḥ sakarmikāyā icchāyāḥ — ca-class of object-bearing will.
dvau ṭavargas tavargaś ca unmeṣāt — double ṭa/ta-class from unmeṣa.
pavargaḥ śaktipañcakayogāt — pa-class from five-power union.
pañcakatvam — hence fivefoldness.
inference: Varga-distribution maps consonant-classes onto the śakti-structure: faith, object-will, awakening, fivefold-union.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What do ya/ra/lā, śa/ṣa/sā, kṣa encode?
premises: icchāyā eva trividhāyā ya ra lāḥ unmeṣāt — of threefold will, ya ra lā from unmeṣa.
vakāraḥ — the va-letter likewise.
icchāyā eva trividhāyāḥ śa ṣa sāḥ visargāt — of threefold will, śa ṣa sā from visarga.
hakāraḥ — the ha-letter likewise.
yonisaṃyogajaḥ kṣakāraḥ — kṣa born of yoni-union.
inference: Each letter-cluster carries its generation-ground: unmeṣa-lineage vs visarga-lineage, kṣa from yoni-conjunction.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What does the scheme identify the Lord as?
premises: ity eṣa bhagavān anuttara eva kuleśvararūpaḥ — thus the Lord is anuttara in kuleśvara-form.
inference: The bīja-analysis terminates in theology: the whole scheme is anuttara-as-kuleśvara.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: How does kaulikī visarga-śakti produce the tattvas?
premises: tasya ekaiva kaulikī visargaśaktiḥ — his one kaulic visarga-power.
yayā ānandarūpāt prabhṛti bahiḥsṛṣṭiparyantena praspandataḥ — throbbing from bliss-form to outer-creation's end.
vargādiparāmarśā eva bahis tattvarūpatāṃ prāptāḥ — class-contemplations outward attain tattva-form.
inference: One kaulic visarga-throb externalizes the varga-parāmarśas into standing tattvas: emanation is visarga-driven.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: How is that visarga threefold?
premises: sa visargas tridhā — the visarga is threefold.
āṇavaḥ cittaviśrāntirūpaḥ — āṇava: form of mind-rest.
śāktaḥ cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ — śākta: marked by mind-awakening.
śāṃbhavaḥ cittapralayarūpaḥ — śāṃbhava: form of mind-dissolution.
inference: The three visarga-modes = the three consciousness-movements: sthiti, saṃbodha, pralaya.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What role does visarga play in world-birth?
premises: evaṃ visarga eva viśvajanane bhagavataḥ śaktiḥ — visarga is the Lord's power in world-birth.
inference: World-generation itself is visarga-operation: the seed-drop, not a separate creator-will.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What happens when parāmarśa is undivided?
premises: yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ — when contemplation is by undividedness alone.
tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā — then the Lord is one, as seed-womb.
bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca — part-wise in contemplation, power-endowed and power.
inference: Undivided = ekatva of Lord and śakti; divided = the śaktimān/śakti dyad — the bīja-yoni keeps both readings.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What do aṣṭaka and ekaika parāmarśas yield?
premises: pṛthak aṣṭakaparāmarśe cakreśvarasāhityena navavargaḥ — separate eightfold, with cakreśvara, nine-class.
ekaikaparāmarśaprādhānye pañcāśadātmakatā — in each-contemplation's prevalence, fiftyfold.
inference: Combinatorics of parāmarśa generate 9 and 50 class-counts: the scheme is generative, not merely classificatory.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What does possible part-difference contemplation yield?
premises: sambhavadbhāgabhedaparāmarśane ekāśītirūpatvam — in contemplation of possible part-difference, eightyfold.
inference: Allowing bheda within sambhavatā raises the count to 80 — numbers track doctrinal permissions.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What is the true count and what does it nourish?
premises: vastutas tu ṣaṭ eva parāmarśāḥ — in reality six contemplations.
prasaraṇapratisaṃcaraṇayogena dvādaśa — by spreading-and-returning, twelve.
parameśvarasya viśvaśaktipūrṇatvaṃ puṣṇanti — they nourish the Lord's world-power fullness.
inference: 6×2=12 is the operative total: the parāmarśas feed the fullness of viśva-śakti, not a larger metaphysics.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What are these powers called?
premises: tā eva etāḥ parāmarśarūpatvāt śaktayo bhagavatyaḥ — those powers, contemplation-formed, are the Lord's.
śrīkālikā iti niruktāḥ — Śrīkālikā they are named.
inference: Parāmarśa-as-śakti = Śrīkālikā: the technical term names the contemplating powers themselves.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: How do pure parāmarśas relate to vidyā/vidyeśvara?
premises: ete śaktirūpā eva śuddhāḥ parāmarśāḥ — these pure contemplations are power-formed.
śuddhavidyāyāṃ parāpararūpatvena — in pure-vidyā by para-apara-form.
māyonmeṣamātrasaṃkocāt — from māyā-awakening's mere contraction.
vidyāvidyeśvararūpatāṃ bhajante — they share vidyā-vidyeśvara-nature.
inference: Purity-condition = para-apara-form in śuddha-vidyā; contraction of māyā-onmeṣa is what splits them into vidyā/vidyeśvara.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: What happens to māyic divisions when re-quickened by pure parāmarśas?
premises: māyāyāṃ sphaṭībhūtabhedavibhāgā māyīyavarṇatāṃ bhajante — in māyā, crystal-formed divisions take māyic letter-nature.
paśyantīmadhyamāvaikharīṣu vyāvahārikatvam āsādya bahīrūpatattvasvabhāvatāpattiparyantāḥ — attaining mundane-status in the three vāk levels up to external-tattva-nature.
uktanayaiḥ śuddhaiḥ parāmarśaiḥ pratyujjīvanaṃ kriyate — revivified by those pure contemplations.
tadā te savīryā bhavanti, bhogamokṣapradāḥ — then vigorous, granting enjoyment and liberation.
sakalaparāmarśaviśrāntimātrarūpaṃ ātmānaṃ paśyato nirvikalpatayā śāṃbhavena samāveśena jīvanmuktatā — seeing self as all-contemplation-rest by śāṃbhava-immersion: liberated-while-living.
inference: Māyic varṇas revive under pure parāmarśa into bhoga-mokṣa-granters; the endpoint is jīvanmuktatā through nirvikalpa śāṃbhava-samāveśa.

speaker: Teacher (parāmarśa-śakti doctrine)
question: Does any mantra-obstruction remain at this level?
premises: atrāpi pūrvavat na mantrādiyantraṇā kācid — here too, as before, no obstruction of mantra and rest.
inference: The letter-scheme operates without mantra-yantraṇa: pure parāmarśa needs no ritual constraint, as before.
